_readme: Adversarial cases for the eight post-processing validators in section 8 of
docs/neurobase-potential-impact-build-spec-v1.0.md.
WRITTEN BEFORE THE VALIDATORS EXIST, ON PURPOSE. Phase 4 accepts when 'all
validation rules in Section 8 fire correctly on constructed adversarial
cases'. If the cases are written alongside the implementation they inherit
its blind spots and the acceptance test becomes a mirror. Every case here is
derived from the SPEC TEXT quoted in `rule_text`, not from any code.
This matters more than usual on this phase. A broken validator does not
produce a broken-looking score. It produces a normal-looking score for an
item that should have been reset, and nothing downstream can tell.
Each case gives:
rule            which section 8 rule it exercises (1-8)
name            what the case is
why             what would go wrong if the validator missed it
input           the ImpactScore fragment fed to the validator
expect          the required outcome after validation
expect.reset    the field that must change, and to what
expect.unchanged true when the validator must NOT fire
Cases marked `must_not_fire` are as important as the ones that must. A
validator that resets everything passes every positive case and destroys the
sort. Roughly half of these exist to catch over-firing.

rules.1: Any dimension score above 0 with an empty or generic `referent` is reset to 0.
rules.2: `LV >= 2` with an empty `beneficiaries` array is reset to 1.
rules.3: `GATE >= 2` with an empty or generic `unlocks` array is reset to 1. Maintain a reject list of generic strings ("advance the field", "help patients", "improve outcomes").
rules.4: `FD > 0` or `GAP > 0` with an empty `frontier_records_consulted` is reset to 0.
rules.5: `FD == 4` without two named paired axes is reset to 3.
rules.6: `record_update_proposed` is discarded if evidence grade is below `demonstrated`.
rules.7: `user_facing_reason` containing rubric vocabulary (dimension names, "score", "rubric", "frontier delta", "leverage") is regenerated. Cap at two attempts, then fall back to a templated sentence from the tags.
rules.8: If `claimed` and `demonstrated` diverge materially, set `gap_flagged: true`.

cases.name: empty referent on a scoring dimension
cases.why: A score with nothing to point at is an unanchored judgement, which is the failure the whole rubric exists to prevent.

cases.name: whitespace-only referent
cases.why: An empty string is the obvious case; a validator that only checks for '' misses the one a model actually emits.

cases.name: missing referent key entirely
cases.why: Absent is not the same as empty, and a validator keyed on `=== ''` lets it through.

cases.name: generic referent that names nothing
cases.why: The spec says empty OR GENERIC. 'the study' points at nothing checkable and is how an unanchored score disguises itself.

cases.name: score of 0 with no referent
cases.why: The rule applies only ABOVE 0. Resetting a 0 is harmless but a validator that fires here is not reading the condition.

cases.name: specific quoted referent
cases.why: The commonest over-fire: a real referent rejected because it is short.

cases.name: LV 2 with no beneficiaries
cases.why: Spec 5.1.2 calls this the anti-hallucination control: if the model cannot name who benefits, it invented the constraint.

cases.name: LV 4 with no beneficiaries
cases.why: The reset target is 1, not 'one less'. A validator that decrements instead of setting 1 leaves a 3 standing.

LV.justification: Changes what is feasible for a device class.

cases.name: LV 2 whose only beneficiary is the authors
cases.why: Spec 5.1.2 requires a party OTHER than the authors. Naming yourself is not leverage.

cases.name: LV 1 with no beneficiaries
cases.why: The rule is LV >= 2. A 1 is defined as a constraint local to the authors, so it needs no external beneficiary.

cases.name: LV 3 with a named external beneficiary
cases.why: Must survive. Over-firing here removes the entire leverage path, which spec 6 says exists to catch the boring-but-important items.

cases.name: GATE 3 with empty unlocks
cases.why: Spec 5.2.2 requires the specific approval, pathway, indication or coverage decision at stake.

cases.name: GATE 2 unlocking 'advance the field'
cases.why: Named verbatim in the spec's reject list. This is the canonical generic entry.

cases.name: GATE 4 unlocking 'help patients'
cases.why: Second entry in the spec's reject list, at the top of the scale where the damage is largest.

cases.name: GATE 3 unlocking 'improve outcomes'
cases.why: Third entry in the spec's reject list.

cases.name: GATE 3 with one generic and one specific unlock
cases.why: A mixed array must survive on the specific entry. Rejecting the whole array because one element is generic destroys a legitimate score.

unlocks: De Novo classification for closed-loop DBS in dystonia

cases.name: GATE 4 with a specific coverage decision
cases.why: Must survive. The gate path is how pivotal trials rank at all.

unlocks: CMS national coverage determination for implanted BCI

cases.name: FD 2 with no records consulted
cases.why: A frontier delta against nothing is not a delta. This is the rule that keeps FD anchored to the record layer.

cases.name: GAP 3 with no records consulted
cases.why: Spec 5.2.1 states it directly: a GAP above 0 with an empty consulted list is rejected.

cases.name: FD 3 on a new axis, records consulted but none matched
cases.why: THE SUBTLE ONE. FD 3 means no record existed for this axis. The consulted list is non-empty (the subfield's records were checked) even though none matched. A validator that reads 'no matching record' as 'no records consulted' makes FD 3 permanently unreachable.

FD.justification: Opens an axis with no prior record.

cases.name: FD 0 with no records consulted
cases.why: Spec 7.1.3 says an empty record set is expected and not a failure. FD is already 0; nothing to reset.

cases.name: LV 3 with no records consulted
cases.why: The rule names FD and GAP only. Leverage does not need a frontier record, and spec 6 depends on the leverage path working when the record layer is empty.

cases.name: FD 4 with no paired axes named
cases.why: Spec 5.1.1: a 4 MUST name both paired axes and why the tradeoff was binding.

cases.name: FD 4 naming only one axis
cases.why: A tradeoff needs two sides. One named axis is an improvement claim, not a collapse.

cases.name: FD 4 naming the same axis twice
cases.why: Two entries that are one axis satisfy a naive length check and are still not a pair.

cases.name: FD 4 with two named axes
cases.why: Must survive, or the top of the frontier scale is unreachable and FD 4 becomes decorative.

FD.justification: Improved channel count without the usual loss of chronic viability.

cases.name: FD 3 with no paired axes
cases.why: The rule applies to FD == 4 only. Requiring a pair at 3 would break 'opens a new axis', which has no pair by definition.

cases.name: record update proposed on a claimed-only item
cases.why: Spec 3.1: claims never update a record. A bad record poisons every later comparison in its subfield.

cases.name: record update proposed on a partial-grade item
cases.why: `partial` is below `demonstrated` in the 5.3.1 table, so it is discarded too.

cases.name: record update proposed on an announced-only trial
cases.why: The trial-variant equivalent of claimed-only, from the 5.3.2 table.

cases.name: record update proposed on a demonstrated item
cases.why: Must survive, or the record layer can never be updated by the pipeline and goes stale. Spec 13 monitors that rate.

cases.name: record update proposed on a replicated item
cases.why: `replicated` is ABOVE demonstrated. A validator comparing strings rather than rank order can easily discard it.

cases.name: reason containing a dimension name
cases.why: Spec 9.1: no dimension names in the user-facing surface. Users would have to learn the rubric to read it.

input.user_facing_reason: Scores highly on frontier delta because it beats the prior record.

cases.name: reason containing the word score
cases.why: Named explicitly in the rule's vocabulary list.

input.user_facing_reason: The highest score in this subfield this year.

cases.name: reason containing the word rubric
cases.why: Named explicitly in the rule's vocabulary list.

input.user_facing_reason: Meets the rubric threshold for a new direction.

cases.name: reason containing leverage as rubric vocabulary
cases.why: Named in the rule. Harder than it looks: see the next case.

input.user_facing_reason: Ranks on leverage rather than on a frontier movement.

cases.name: reason using leverage as ordinary English
cases.why: THE TRAP. A blanket substring ban on 'leverage' rejects a plain-language sentence that is exactly what section 9.2 asks for. The rule bans rubric VOCABULARY, not English words.

input.user_facing_reason: The technique leverages existing surgical tooling, so no new instrument is needed.

cases.name: a clean plain-language reason
cases.why: Taken from the register examples in spec 9.2. Must survive untouched.

input.user_facing_reason: Roughly doubles reported chronic electrode viability compared with the previous best in this class.

cases.name: regeneration exhausts its two attempts
cases.why: The rule caps at two attempts then falls back to a templated sentence from the tags. Without the cap this loops forever on a stubborn model.

cases.name: claim with nothing demonstrated
cases.why: Spec 5.3.3: if an item announces a capability and shows data for a weaker one, score the weaker and set gap_flagged.

cases.name: claim materially exceeding what was shown
cases.why: The substantive case: both fields are populated but they are not the same claim.

input.claimed: Restores natural speech in people with paralysis.
input.demonstrated: Decoded 62 words per minute from a 50-word vocabulary in one participant.

cases.name: claim matching what was shown
cases.why: Must NOT fire. If gap_flagged fires on everything it stops distinguishing anything, and the disclosure tags in 9.2 become noise.

input.claimed: Decoded 62 words per minute in one participant.
input.demonstrated: Decoded 62 words per minute in one participant with ALS.

cases.name: registered trial that has not reported
cases.why: A trial demonstrates nothing yet BY DEFINITION. Spec 5.2.4 handles trial quality through the design-quality grade, not through this flag. Firing here flagged 6 of 8 sampled trials during Phase 3.

input.claimed: Will test whether closed-loop stimulation reduces seizure frequency.
input.demonstrated: A randomized sham-controlled design able to establish whether closed-loop stimulation reduces seizure frequency in drug-resistant epilepsy.
